text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Baster community has finally dropped its claims on land at Rehoboth. The move brings to an end an often bitter seven-year legal dispute between the Baster community and the central government over land ownership in the Rehoboth district, which has been a major discouragement to investment in the area.
- A group of up to 40 Brazilian sailors are alleged to have attacked Namibians at a Walvis Bay pub.
- The five members of the Southern African Customs Union have been accused by other members of the Southern African Development Community of blocking the ratification of a free trade protocol.
- A third cooperation agreement in the fisheries sector has been signed between Namibia and Norway, bringing in N$90 million in financial support and three more years of research cooporation.

- The Baster leader, the prime minister and the attorney-general were the main players an emotional meeting in Rehoboth, where the local people decided to put aside their long-standing political differences for the sake of development of the whole of the community.
